payload.description_html:
Otodus obliquus Agassiz, 1838 - fossil mackerel shark tooth from the Eocene of Morocco.

Normal specimens of this kind of shark tooth are not sharply-hooked. The morphology is some type of malformation, possibly resulting from an injury.

Exhibit info.:

Otodus obiquus Agassiz, 1838 Eocene Khouribga Phosphates Khouribga, Morocco

Sharks with an injured jaw may produce uncommon "pathological" teeth, with twisted, bent, or split cusps, such as these examples.

Classification: Animalia, Chordata, Vertebrata, Chondritchthyes, Elasmobranchii, Lamniformes, Otodontidae

Stratigraphy: Khouribga Phosphates, Eocene

Locality: unrecorded / undisclosed site at or near the town of Khouribga (probably from a phosphate mine), Morocco
